title: The Minimal Atoms
summary: This document demonstrates that reflections alone generate all plane isometries (needing at most three), then extends this principle across mathematics, logic, computation, and biology: minimal generating sets produce infinite structural consequences. It provides a rigorous geometric proof as the anchor example and maps the pattern to NAND gates, prime factorization, Fourier bases, permutation groups, one-instruction computers, and trichromatic vision.
compress: A finite set of irreducible operations can generate an entire operational universe; identifying these true generative atoms is the deepest understanding, and this claim crosses from philosophy to science when converted into falsifiable experiments — a conversion now concretely instantiated with synthetic ground truth, agent architectures, and formal metrics testing whether reasoning equals compressive prediction.
invariants: Active inference outperforms passive observation as a structural prediction
Philosophical claims require experimental bridges to constitute knowledge
The reasoning-as-compression thesis has a concrete experimental instantiation
Structure is the only carrier of meaning
Falsifiability is the membrane between generative theory and generative science
Recursive self-improvement is bounded by epistemic humility
Theoretical claims gain epistemic weight proportional to the specificity of their falsification protocols
obligations: Track experimental outcomes against the prediction that active-inference agents outperform passive observers on compressive prediction tasks
Evaluate whether the synthetic ground truth methodology generalizes beyond the initial experimental design
Compression-as-reasoning must be tested across multiple agent architectures to confirm substrate independence
The minimal atoms framework must specify what experimental outcome would disconfirm its own irreducibility claims
